practiceQuestions.q: On whose recommendation was the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) originally established in 1964?
practiceQuestions.sol: The CVC was set up in 1964 by an executive resolution of the Central Government on the recommendation of the Committee on Prevention of Corruption, chaired by K. Santhanam.

practiceQuestions.q: In which year did the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) attain statutory status?
practiceQuestions.sol: Parliament enacted the Central Vigilance Commission Act in 2003, giving statutory status to the CVC following the Supreme Court directions in the Vineet Narain case.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the maximum number of Vigilance Commissioners that can be appointed in the CVC apart from the Central Vigilance Commissioner?
practiceQuestions.sol: According to the CVC Act 2003, the Commission consists of a Central Vigilance Commissioner (Chairperson) and not more than two Vigilance Commissioners (members).

practiceQuestions.q: Who heads the high-level committee that recommends the appointment of the Central Vigilance Commissioner?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Central Vigilance Commissioner and Vigilance Commissioners are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee headed by the Prime Minister, along with the Minister of Home Affairs and the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the tenure of office for the Central Vigilance Commissioner?
opts: 3 years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
4 years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
5 years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
5 years or 62 years of age, whichever is earlier
practiceQuestions.sol: The CVC and Vigilance Commissioners hold office for a term of 4 years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.

practiceQuestions.q: Can the Central Vigilance Commissioner or Vigilance Commissioners be re-appointed to the same office after completing their tenure?
opts: Yes, with the consent of Parliament
No, they are not eligible for further employment under the Central or State Government
Yes, if recommended by the UPSC
practiceQuestions.sol: Once they complete their tenure, the Central Vigilance Commissioner and Vigilance Commissioners are not eligible for further employment under the Central or State Government.

practiceQuestions.q: To whom does the Central Vigilance Commission submit its annual report regarding its performance?
practiceQuestions.sol: The CVC presents an annual report on its performance to the President of India, who places it before each House of Parliament.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following agencies acts as the investigative arm of the Central Vigilance Commission for anti-corruption cases?
practiceQuestions.sol: The CVC exercises superintendence over the functioning of the CBI in respect of investigation of offenses under the Prevention of Corruption Act.

practiceQuestions.q: Under the CVC Act, what role does the Commission play regarding the Delhi Special Police Establishment (CBI)?
opts: Superintendence of CBI investigation for corruption cases
Appointing the Director of CBI exclusively
practiceQuestions.sol: The CVC has been assigned the power to exercise superintendence over the CBI's investigation into offenses under the Prevention of Corruption Act.

practiceQuestions.q: Whistle Blowers Protection Act operationalizes which mechanism through the CVC?
opts: Public Interest Disclosure and Protection of Informers (PIDPI) resolution
Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS)
practiceQuestions.sol: The CVC is designated as the agency to receive complaints relating to disclosure on any allegation of corruption or willful misuse of power and to safeguard complainants under the PIDPI resolution.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the removal process of the Central Vigilance Commissioner safeguard institutional independence?
opts: The President can remove them at any time without assigning reasons.
Removal can only happen on the ground of proved misbehavior or incapacity after a Supreme Court inquiry.
Removal requires a two-thirds majority resolution passed by the Lok Sabha only.
They can be removed by the Prime Minister's direct executive order.
practiceQuestions.sol: To ensure independence, the President can only remove the CVC or a Vigilance Commissioner on the ground of proved misbehavior or incapacity, and that too only after the Supreme Court, on a reference made to it by the President, has reported in an inquiry that they ought to be removed.

practiceQuestions.q: In what scenario can the President suspend the Central Vigilance Commissioner or a Vigilance Commissioner pending an inquiry?
opts: When a criminal charge is filed against them in a subordinate court.
When the President has referred the matter of removal to the Supreme Court.
When the Prime Minister recommends suspension due to policy differences.
When Parliament passes a no-confidence motion against the Commission.
practiceQuestions.sol: The President may suspend the CVC or any Vigilance Commissioner from office in respect of whom a reference has been made to the Supreme Court until the President has passed orders on the Supreme Court's report.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary jurisdictional scope of the CVC regarding central government employees?
opts: All employees across Central and State governments indiscriminately.
Members of All-India Services and Group A officers of the Central Government.
Only clerical and Group C/D staff of Union Ministries.
Private corporate executives receiving public funds.
practiceQuestions.sol: The CVC exercises jurisdiction over members of All-India Services serving in connection with the affairs of the Union and Group A officers of the Central Government, along with specified public sector undertakings, banks, and autonomous bodies.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the establishment of the Lokpal impact the functional dynamics of the Central Vigilance Commission?
opts: It completely subsumes and abolishes the CVC.
Lokpal can refer preliminary inquiry cases involving Group A/B officers to the CVC.
The CVC takes over all judicial powers of the Lokpal.
There is no statutory link or operational overlap between Lokpal and CVC.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, the Lokpal can refer complaints against Group A and B officers to the CVC for a preliminary inquiry, and the CVC submits its report back to the Lokpal.

practiceQuestions.q: Why was the 'Single Directive' provision related to the CBI a major point of contention concerning the CVC?
opts: It forced the CBI to investigate all petty crimes without CVC permission.
It required prior approval of the Central Government before initiating inquiry against joint secretary level and above officers, which the Supreme Court struck down.
It allowed the CVC to suspend the CBI Director arbitrarily.
It banned the CBI from probing private financial institutions.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the nature of the CVC's recommendations to government departments on disciplinary matters?
opts: Binding on all departments in all circumstances.
Advisory in nature, though departments must consult CVC and report deviations.
Purely judicial rulings that can be appealed only in the Supreme Court.
Non-binding suggestions with no requirement for departments to explain non-compliance.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the CVC ensure vigilance administration in Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) and Public Sector Banks (PSBs)?
opts: Through Chief Vigilance Officers (CVOs) appointed in each organization.
By deploying dedicated CVC paramilitary units inside every bank branch.
By conducting mandatory daily audits of all financial transactions.
By replacing the board of directors with CVC nominees.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the significance of the Integrity Index introduced by the CVC?
opts: It measures the GDP loss due to corruption in states.
It benchmarks internal processes and controls of organizations to promote systemic anti-corruption measures.
It acts as a credit rating scale for private multinational corporations.
It ranks individual citizens based on their tax compliance history.

practiceQuestions.q: Which constitutional or legal limitation does the CVC face when dealing with allegations against ministers or political executives directly?
opts: CVC has absolute jurisdiction to prosecute ministers without executive sanction.
CVC's direct investigative mandate is restricted primarily to bureaucratic officials, while allegations against ministers often involve the Lokpal or specific constitutional safeguards.
CVC acts as a special court for trying corrupt ministers.
Ministers are completely immune from any anti-corruption oversight.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the CVC referred to as an apex anti-corruption body despite not having its own dedicated police investigating cadre?
opts: Because it holds legislative power to make anti-corruption laws.
Because it exercises overarching superintendence and policy direction over central vigilance administration and CBI's anti-corruption wing.
Because it directly controls all state vigilance commissions.
Because it has the power to dismiss elected governments.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC):
1. It was originally established in 1964 by an executive resolution of the Government of India.
2. It became a statutory body following the enactment of the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The CVC was set up in 1964 on Santhanam Committee recommendations as an executive body and was later given statutory backing via the CVC Act, 2003.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition of the CVC:
1. The Commission consists of a Central Vigilance Commissioner and not more than four Vigilance Commissioners.
2. Members are appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the CVC consists of a Central Vigilance Commissioner and *not more than two* Vigilance Commissioners (not four). Statement 2 is correct; appointment is made by the President under his hand and seal.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the selection committee for the Central Vigilance Commissioner:
1. The committee is headed by the Prime Minister.
2. The Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha is a member of this committee.
3. The Union Minister of Home Affairs is a member of this committee.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (PM heads it). Statement 3 is correct (Home Minister is a member). Statement 2 is incorrect because the committee includes the Leader of the Opposition in the *Lok Sabha*, not the Rajya Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the tenure and service conditions of the CVC:
1. The term of office is 5 years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
2. They are eligible for re-appointment to the Central Vigilance Commission after completing their first term.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. The tenure is 4 years (not 5 years) or 65 years of age. Furthermore, they are *not* eligible for re-appointment under the Central or State Government.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the functions and powers of the CVC:
1. It can conduct investigations suo motu into any corruption complaint against any public servant without governmental sanction.
2. It exercises superintendence over the CBI in investigations conducted under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the CVC does not conduct investigations itself; it gets inquiries done through the CBI or Chief Vigilance Officers. Statement 2 is correct: it exercises superintendence over the CBI regarding anti-corruption cases.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the removal of the Central Vigilance Commissioner:
1. The President can remove the CVC on the ground of proved misbehavior only after the Supreme Court holds an inquiry and recommends it.
2. The President can also remove the CVC if the CVC is adjudged an insolvent or engages in paid employment outside official duties.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. While proved misbehavior requires a Supreme Court inquiry, the President can remove the CVC directly without SC reference if adjudged insolvent, convicted of an offense involving moral turpitude, or engaged in paid employment outside duties.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the jurisdiction of the CVC:
1. It has jurisdiction over all employees of the Union government, including Group C and Group D workers directly.
2. It has the authority to review pending corruption cases of departments and advise on disciplinary actions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because CVC's core direct jurisdiction covers All-India Services and Group A officers of the Centre, along with senior executives of PSUs/Banks, not directly all Group C and D employees. Statement 2 is correct; it reviews pending vigilance cases and advises departments.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Whistle Blowers Protection Act and the CVC:
1. The CVC is designated as the competent authority to receive complaints relating to disclosure on corruption or misuse of office.
2. The CVC has the power to reveal the identity of the complainant if it deems necessary for investigation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; CVC acts as the competent authority under PIDPI. Statement 2 is incorrect because the CVC is legally mandated to protect the identity of the complainant and cannot reveal it except under very strict judicial or statutory mandates, ensuring strict confidentiality.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the reporting accountability of the CVC:
1. The CVC submits its annual report to the Prime Minister, who then presents it to the Cabinet.
2. The report details the performance of the Commission as well as cases where advice of the CVC was not accepted by departments.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the CVC submits its annual report to the *President of India*, not the Prime Minister. Statement 2 is correct: the report highlights cases of non-acceptance of CVC advice by ministries or departments.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the independence of the Central Vigilance Commission:
1. The salaries, allowances, and other conditions of service of the Central Vigilance Commissioner are akin to those of the Chairman of UPSC.
2. The expenses of the CVC are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: the CVC's salary is equivalent to that of the UPSC Chairman (and Vigilance Commissioners are equivalent to UPSC members). Statement 2 is incorrect because the administrative expenses of the CVC are *not* charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India; rather, they are voted upon by Parliament.
